paper.title_en: Tentative Excess Dispersion Measures toward DESI Galaxy Groups from Localized Fast Radio Bursts
paper.abstract_en: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) provide sensitive probes of ionized baryons through their dispersion measures (DMs). In this work, we test whether localized FRB sight lines intersecting foreground galaxy groups exhibit a measurable excess in cosmic DM relative to clean nonintersecting sight lines. We crossmatch 117 localized FRBs with measured DMs and host redshifts against a foreground group catalog from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys. Within the catalog footprint and at $z_{\rm host}<0.5$, we identify 23 sight lines intersecting foreground groups and 18 clean nonintersecting sight lines for the main comparison. A joint fit to this sample gives a positive offset of $143.3^{+53.2}_{-53.0}~\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ in the inferred cosmic DM, $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm cosmic}$, for the group-intersecting sight lines relative to the nonintersecting control sample. A template fit for the foreground halos gives $A_{\rm halo}=0.34^{+0.51}_{-0.50}$, with a positive posterior median but a weakly constrained detailed halo contribution. A mock forecast within the DESI footprint indicates that larger samples of localized FRBs would improve the foreground halo template constraint.
